facts: Source identifies deforestation, firewood demand, livestock pressure and road construction as environmental challenges.
It connects disturbed slopes with soil erosion and landslides.
Source distinguishes ordinary, mineral and thermal water springs.
It describes hot springs as naturally fluctuating water sources and notes their mineral content and cultural/medicinal significance.
Source discusses geologically fragile terrain in the Sutlej basin.
A catchment treatment plan is described, including stabilization of identified landslide points and bioengineering measures.
Soil erosion and sediment entering reservoirs are presented as key issues.
Source links degradation to river-bank cultivation, vegetation removal, erosion, flood-water spill and pressure on land resources.
Channelisation and watershed treatment are discussed.
Source describes Bara Shigri as the largest glacier in Himachal Pradesh.
Located in the Chandra valley and feeding the Chenab system.
Source gives approximately 25 km length and discusses its large ice cover.

facts: Source reproduces a 1999 state notification concerning areas treated as difficult/inaccessible for administrative transfer and placement purposes.
It lists areas in Kinnaur, Lahaul-Spiti, Chamba, Sirmaur, Kangra, Mandi, Shimla and Kullu.
Source states that a one-member commission was set up in June 2011 concerning benami land deals and related land/property legislation.
It describes interim and final reports issued in 2012.
Source discusses a 2008 re-notification and lists areas treated as tribal under the cited notification.
Some place names are damaged by OCR and should be checked against the original document.
Source reports Himachal being declared smoke-free in 2013 and gives compliance percentages from a cited survey.
It also discusses smoking prevalence among youth.
Source mentions a spring near Baijnath.

asni.name: Asni

baira.name: Baira

Source says it is substantially rain-fed and has formed broad terraces.

bata.name: Bata

facts: Source gives total length about 460 km.

beas.name: Beas

facts: Rises in the Bara Banghal area between the Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar ranges.
Joins the Tant Gari to form the Ravi mainstream.
Catchment includes U-shaped valleys, waterfalls, moraines and cirques.
bhadal.name: Bhadal

facts: Included among the principal Himalayan rivers connected with Himachal's drainage system.
The source connects the Chandra and Bhaga system with the Chenab around Tandi.
chenab.name: Chenab

facts: Important tributary of the Yamuna system.
Source says it rises near Kupor/Kuper peak in the Jubbal-Rohru hills, flows through the Shimla hills and divides the Sirmaur region into Cis-Giri and Trans-Giri.
Joins the Yamuna system near Paonta.
giri.name: Giri

facts: Small rain-fed tributary described as rising from the Dharthi ranges.
Joins the Giri near Dadahu according to the source.
jalal.name: Jalal

facts: Small river rising from the southern face of the low Shivalik/Markanda area.
Associated with the Kiarda-dun/Paonta valley and Nahan region.
Source notes low winter/summer flow and sharp monsoon rise.
markanda.name: Markanda

facts: Tributary of the Tons, which joins the Yamuna system.
Source connects its headwaters with the Dhauladhar/upper Himalayan area and the Chandra Nahan glacier.
Flows through the Rohru-Chirgaon region.
pabbar.name: Pabbar

facts: Source describes the Ravi as a major river of Chamba and says it eventually joins the Chenab in Pakistan.
Important settlements named include Bharmaur, Madhopur and Chamba.
Source gives total length about 720 km.
ravi.name: Ravi

facts: Source describes its entry into Himachal near Shipki and course through Kinnaur, Shimla, Kullu, Mandi and Bilaspur regions.
Important tributaries listed include Spiti, Baspa, Tait/possibly Taiti, Kupa, Kanhang, Yula, Wangar, Throng and Rupi, with additional left-bank tributaries.
Bhakra is described as a major dam on the river.
Important settlements named include Namgia, Kalpa, Rampur, Tattapani and Bilaspur.
satluj.name: Satluj

facts: Tributary of the Ravi.
Rises near the Himachal–Jammu border area and is fed by snowmelt and springs.
Baira is identified as a prominent tributary.
siul.name: Siul

facts: Source describes the Swan catchment in the lower Shivaliks as environmentally degraded and in need of restoration.
Agricultural expansion, river-bank cultivation, erosion, flooding and loss of vegetation are discussed.
Source states that the river has 73 tributaries and describes a channelisation programme.
swan-river.name: Swan River

facts: Rises east of Bharmaur.
Merges with Bhadal to form the Ravi mainstream.
Source describes a U-shaped valley with glacial/morainic deposits.
tant-gari.name: Tant Gari

facts: Source describes the Yamuna drainage and its Himachal tributary network, including the Giri, Pabbar/Tons system and Bata.
The river continues through Uttarakhand, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh.
yamuna.name: Yamuna

Source describes agricultural land and an Indo-German agriculture project.
balh-valley.name: Balh Valley

facts: Lies between the Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal ranges.
Partly in Kangra and partly in Chamba according to the source.
Source says the Ravi rises from its slopes.
bara-banghal-valley.name: Bara Banghal Valley

facts: Also referred to as the Ravi valley in the source.
Known for varied landscapes, terraces, forests, medicinal herbs and flowers.

chamba-valley.name: Chamba Valley

facts: Mentioned as adjoining the Kiarda-dun valley.

dun-and-sproon-valleys.name: Dun and Sproon Valleys

facts: Dun-type valley between the Dhauladhar and Shivalik hills.

Source highlights Kangra paintings, historical finds, forts, temples and galleries.
kangra-valley.name: Kangra Valley

facts: Also called Paonta Valley in the source.
Associated with Markanda and Dharthi ranges and the Yamuna.
Source divides it into Neli Khera, Par-dun and Dun Proper tracts.
Giri and Bata are described as important waters.
kiarda-dun-valley.name: Kiarda-dun Valley

facts: Broad valley formed by the Beas between Mandi and the Kullu/Manali region.
Source emphasizes its landscape, settlements, cultural character and hot springs.
kullu-valley.name: Kullu Valley

facts: Lies north of the Pir Panjal and main Himalayan ranges.
Formed by the Chandra and Bhaga rivers up to Tandi and Chenab downstream.
Source highlights severe winter and off-season vegetable/seed-potato cultivation.
lahaul-valley.name: Lahaul Valley

facts: Described as extending along the Chenab as it cuts through the Pir Panjal and main Himalayan ranges.
Characterized in the source as remote and scenic.
pangi-valley.name: Pangi Valley

facts: Runs from Shipki toward Bilaspur along the Satluj.
Source says the river cuts across major Himalayan ranges and identifies Bilaspur, Rampur and Bhaba among settlements.
Source also discusses landslide stabilization and catchment treatment.
satluj-valley.name: Satluj Valley

facts: Formed by the Spiti river and located between the main Himalaya and Zanskar ranges.
Kaza is identified as a principal town.
Source gives surrounding elevations broadly between 3,000 and 6,500 m.
spiti-valley.name: Spiti Valley
